notes.22v.22a: hana galdr, 'the crowing of cocks', uses galdr, the usual word for a chanted spell.

nodes.text: thus all alone, she heard very
far off on her right hand the barking of dogs
and the crowing of cocks,
and she knew from that that there must surely be a farm there,
and
tales of lays and of string-music,
then I will not forget
Bisclaret. Bisclaret was
a knight, valiant
and courteous, bold with weapons and strong. Bisclaret he was called
in the Breton
tongue, but the Normans called him *vargulf* [werewolf]. In olden times
one could hear of what often might happen: that
many
men changed their shapes and became wolves and lived in
forests and in woods,
and there they had houses and mighty dwellings. And a *vargulf*
was a wild beast while
going to confession avails nothing for those who will not
give up
their sins. So you imagine that I mean to work
spells on you
with wickedness. But I am not that kind of
evil creature. When you go to
church to pray
for yourself, then you shall see me stand beside you and
take consecrated bread with you. But you have greatly
wronged me. But I
have loved you too much.
